issues.description: The rule requires that classes interacting with UIKit or performing UI updates must be marked with @MainActor annotation. The SettingsTextFormatter class formats text for UI display in settings screens but lacks the @MainActor annotation.

issues.title: Incorrect localized string reference in SettingsTextFormatter
issues.description: The formatStudiesText method references strings.detailTextStudies instead of strings.detailTextStudiesV2. This causes the formatter to display the old v1 Studies message ('%@ may install and run studies from time to time.') instead of the new v148 message ('%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.') that was added in this PR. The helper class was clearly intended to format the new v148 strings based on the PR context, but uses the wrong string constant.

issues.title: Inconsistent format specifier documentation in RolloutsSettingMessage comment
issues.description: The comment for RolloutsSettingMessage incorrectly documents the format specifier as '%1$@' (positional format) while the actual value string uses '%@' (simple format). This mismatch creates confusion for localization teams and could lead to incorrect translations, as translators may attempt to use positional formatting based on the comment when the string implementation doesn't support it. The comment should match the actual format specifier used in the value field.

issues.title: Linter exclusion points to wrong message key version
issues.description: The linter configuration exclusion was updated to reference 'Settings.Studies.Message.v148' but the original PR added this key to exclude quotes validation for the v136 message. Since the PR adds new v148 strings with similar content containing quotes, the exclusion should have remained as v136 to maintain the existing exclusion, or both versions should be excluded. This change will cause the linter to fail validation on the v136 string that legitimately needs the exclusion, while potentially missing issues in the new v148 string.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter class missing final keyword
issues.description: The newly added SettingsTextFormatter class violates repository Rule #12 from AGENTS.md, which requires classes that are not designed for subclassing to be marked with the 'final' keyword. This helper class is clearly not intended for inheritance (it has a private initializer and is a simple utility class), but lacks the final modifier. This prevents compiler optimizations and fails to communicate design intent explicitly, violating an explicit compliance rule added in this same PR.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter and its methods lack explicit access control
issues.description: Rule requires explicit access control modifiers. The new nested class and its members use default (implicit) access levels (`class`, `static let shared`, and `func` declarations have no explicit `internal`/`private`/`public`).
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter should be marked final
issues.description: The helper singleton class is not designed for inheritance but is declared as a non-final class. Per the rule, such classes must be marked `final` to prevent unintended subclassing and enable compiler optimizations.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: EXP-5874 Add strings for Rollouts toggle and update Studies strings

structured_output.summary:
This PR is localization prep for the v148 "Studies/Rollouts" settings split (foundation for mozilla-mobile/firefox-ios#30988). On the firefox-ios side it adds six new `MZLocalizedString` entries in `Shared/Strings.swift` — v148 Studies Title/Link/Message plus new Rollouts Title/Link/Message — and mirrors those keys/values into the developer-maintained `en-CA`/`en-GB` `Settings.strings` source locales. On the focus-ios side it adds matching `NSLocalizedString` constants (`labelStudiesV2`, `detailTextStudiesV2`, `labelRollouts`, `detailTextRollouts`, plus a `detailTextSendUsageDataV2`). It also updates the l10n `quotes` linter exclusion.

The strings themselves are correct and internally consistent: every `MZLocalizedString` key matches its `en-CA`/`en-GB` counterpart, values line up, and the `%@` app-name placeholder is preserved. The concern is the head commit (`a606e5ba` "update pr"), which also adds a `SettingsTextFormatter` helper class to focus-ios `UIConstants` that is never wired into the settings screen and uses the old (v1) studies string — out of scope for a strings-only PR and dead on arrival. Two smaller nits (a duplicated `detailTextSendUsageDataV2` and an inconsistent `%1$@` vs `%@` in one comment) round out the review.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The core deliverable — the v148 Studies and Rollouts strings for both firefox-ios and focus-ios — is correct and ready. However, the head commit introduces a non-string `SettingsTextFormatter` class that is unused, duplicates the existing inline formatting pattern in `SettingsViewController`, and references the v1 studies string instead of the v2 string this PR adds. That is dead code that shouldn't ship in a strings PR; it should be removed (or wired up with the v2 strings) before merge. A duplicate constant and a comment/placeholder mismatch are minor cleanups.

architecture.overview:
firefox-ios localizes via `MZLocalizedString(key, tableName, value, comment)` constants in `Shared/Strings.swift`, with the developer-maintained source strings in `en-CA.lproj/Settings.strings` and `en-GB.lproj/Settings.strings` serving as the translator source of truth; each Swift constant's `key` must match an entry in those `.strings` files. focus-ios (the separate Focus app in the same monorepo) localizes differently — `NSLocalizedString` with an inline `value:` default inside the `UIConstants.strings` nested struct, so no `.strings` file edits are needed there. The live settings screen (`SettingsViewController`) builds each toggle's subtitle inline via `String(format: UIConstants.strings.detailTextStudies, AppInfo.productName)`.

This PR adds the v148 Studies strings and the brand-new Rollouts strings on both sides, plus a `quotes` linter exclusion for the v148 Studies message. The head commit additionally adds a `UIConstants.SettingsTextFormatter` class with a `shared` singleton and two `format…Text(appName:)` helpers — but this class is not connected to `SettingsViewController`, which still uses the inline pattern, so the new abstraction sits outside the actual display path.
steps: firefox-ios: `Shared/Strings.swift` adds six `MZLocalizedString` constants keyed `Settings.Studies.{Title,Link,Message}.v148` and `Settings.Rollouts.{Title,Link,Message}.v148` (`StudiesSettingTitleV3`/`LinkV3`/`MessageV3` + `RolloutsSettingTitle`/`Link`/`Message`).
firefox-ios: `en-CA.lproj/Settings.strings` and `en-GB.lproj/Settings.strings` mirror those six keys/values for the two source locales (translator source of truth).
l10n config: `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json` adds `firefox-ios.xliff:Settings.Studies.Message.v148` to the `quotes` exclusion list.

focus-ios: `UIConstants.strings` adds `labelStudiesV2`, `detailTextStudiesV2`, `labelRollouts`, `detailTextRollouts`, and a verbatim `detailTextSendUsageDataV2`, plus a nested `SettingsTextFormatter` class (head commit).

Display path: `SettingsViewController.initializeToggles()` still builds the Studies toggle subtitle inline at line 127 (`String(format: UIConstants.strings.detailTextStudies, AppInfo.productName)`); the new `SettingsTextFormatter` is not referenced from this or any other call site.

findings.title: SettingsTextFormatter is unused dead code that uses the v1 studies string
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`, the new `SettingsTextFormatter` class (lines 417-430) is never called anywhere in the repo and this PR is strings-only prep for the Studies/Rollouts split. The live settings screen (`focus-ios/Blockzilla/Settings/Controller/SettingsViewController.swift` line 127) already formats the subtitle inline via `String(format: UIConstants.strings.detailTextStudies, AppInfo.productName)`. Remove the `SettingsTextFormatter` class entirely. If a shared formatter is genuinely wanted, add it as a `static func` on the `strings` struct AND wire `SettingsViewController` to use it, and have it use `detailTextStudiesV2` (the v148 text this PR adds), not `detailTextStudies` (the v1 text). Don't ship an unused singleton class.
findings.body:
The head commit adds `UIConstants.SettingsTextFormatter` — a `class` with a `shared` singleton and two `format…Text(appName:)` helpers — but nothing calls it. `formatStudiesText` / `formatRolloutsText` appear only at their definition; the settings screen still builds its subtitle inline the same way it always has:

::code{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/Settings/Controller/SettingsViewController.swift" lines="127-128"}

::diff{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift" lines="417-430"}

::callout{type="warning"
This PR is described as strings-only prep for the Studies/Rollouts split (#30988). A non-string helper class — especially one that isn't wired into the screen it claims to serve — is out of scope and will rot the instant the real UI work lands with its own formatting approach.

There's also a latent correctness trap: `formatStudiesText` formats `strings.detailTextStudies`, the **v1** text "%@ may install and run studies from time to time.", not the `detailTextStudiesV2` ("%@ randomly selects users to test features…") that this PR adds for v148. If anyone ever connects this formatter, the Studies toggle would display the old copy and silently undo the string update this PR exists to ship.

For a stateless formatter, prefer a `static func` on the `strings` struct over a `class` + `shared` singleton — and if kept, wire it into `SettingsViewController` and point it at the v2 strings.

findings.title: detailTextSendUsageDataV2 is a verbatim duplicate of detailTextSendUsageData
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`, `detailTextSendUsageDataV2` (line 203) has the exact same `value` and `comment` as `detailTextSendUsageData` (line 202), just re-keyed `Settings.detailTextSendUsageData.v2`, and it has no callers. If the v2 copy is meant to differ from v1, update its `value`; otherwise delete `detailTextSendUsageDataV2` so there's a single source of truth for the Send Usage Data description.
findings.body:
The new `detailTextSendUsageDataV2` has the identical `value` and `comment` to the existing `detailTextSendUsageData`, just re-keyed with `.v2`, and nothing references it.

::diff{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift" lines="202-203"}

::callout{type="info"
It's also unrelated to the Studies/Rollouts split this PR is about. If the v2 text is genuinely meant to differ, update the value; if not, drop the duplicate so there's a single source of truth for the Send Usage Data description.

findings.title: RolloutsSettingMessage comment documents %1$@ but the value uses %@
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`, the `RolloutsSettingMessage` constant (lines 6257-6261) has `value` "%@ will improve features…" but its `comment` says "%1$@ is the app name". The sibling `StudiesSettingMessageV3` documents `%@` in both. Revert the comment to "%@ is the app name (e.g. Firefox)." so the documented placeholder matches the actual `%@` format specifier and stays consistent with the Studies string in the same diff.

findings.title: quotes linter exclusion targets a string with no quote characters
findings.fixPrompt: In `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json`, the `quotes.exclusions` entry (lines 8-10) was changed from `Settings.Studies.Message.v136` to `Settings.Studies.Message.v148`. The v148 value ("%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.") has no quotes/apostrophes, whereas the v136 value ("…before they're released to everyone.") contains a curly apostrophe and is the string that historically needed the exclusion. Verify with the l10n team which key should carry the `quotes` exclusion; if v136 still needs it, keep v136 (and add v148 only if actually required), so the apostrophe-bearing v136 message doesn't silently lose its exclusion.
findings.body:
The `quotes` exclusion now points at `Settings.Studies.Message.v148`, whose value is "%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone." — it contains no quotation marks or apostrophes. The previous v136 message ("…before they’re released to everyone.") does contain a curly apostrophe and is the string that historically carried this exclusion.

::diff{file=".github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json" lines="8-10"}

::callout{type="warning"
A `quotes`-category exclusion is for quote/apostrophe handling, so excluding v148 looks like a no-op while v136 (which has the apostrophe) loses its coverage. Confirm with l10n which key should carry the exclusion; if it's still v136, the head commit moved it off the string that actually needs it.

findings.title: firefox-ios v148 strings are mirrored correctly across Swift and both source locales
findings.body: The six new `MZLocalizedString` entries in `Shared/Strings.swift` (`StudiesSettingTitleV3`/`LinkV3`/`MessageV3` + `RolloutsSettingTitle`/`Link`/`Message`) are mirrored exactly in both `en-CA.lproj/Settings.strings` and `en-GB.lproj/Settings.strings` — keys match (`Settings.Studies.Title.v148`, `Settings.Rollouts.Message.v148`, etc.), values match, and the `%@` app-name placeholder is preserved in both the Swift `value` and the `.strings` entries. Clean, consistent l10n setup for the v148 split.
